title: Chapter 1. Padas Dated to the Lord's Lifetime (after Majumdar)
html:
Padas by Sri Chaitanya's companions which Bimanbihari Majumdar (Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan, ch. 2) assigns to the Lord's lifetime, arranged in the order of events: from Nimai's journey to East Bengal, through the Navadvipa kirtanas of 1509 and the sannyasa, to the first years of separation (the padas of the Puri period follow in the next chapter). The text follows the Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Govinda Ghosha — "gorā gelā pūrvadeśa…" (PK 1597)

Lila: Vishvambhara in East Bengal; in Navadvipa His dear ones pine for Him. According to Majumdar it was composed while the Lord was away, before Gaya: if so, it is the earliest surviving pada about Gaura. Raga pahida.1

গোরা গেলা পূর্বদেশ নিজগণ পাই ক্লেশ
বিলাপয়ে কত পরকার ।
কান্দে দেবী লক্ষ্মীপ্রিয়া শুনিতে বিদরে হিয়া
দিবসে মানয়ে অন্ধকার ॥

gorā gelā pūrvadeśa nijagaṇa pāi kleśa
bilāpaye kata parakāra |
kānde debī lakṣmīpriyā śunite bidare hiyā
dibase mānaye andhakāra ||

gora gela purvadesha — Gora went to the Eastern land; nijagana pai klesha — His own people, in anguish; bilapaye kata parakara — lament in so many ways; kande devi lakshmipriya — Devi Lakshmipriya weeps; shunite bidare hiya — to hear it the heart breaks; dibase manaye andhakara — by day she sees darkness

1.1Gora has gone to the Eastern land, and His own people, in anguish,
lament in so many ways.
Devi Lakshmipriya weeps — to hear it the heart breaks;
broad day is darkness to her.2

হরি হরি গৌরাঙ্গ-বিচ্ছেদ নাহি সহে ।
পুন সেই গোরা-মুখ দেখিয়া ঘুচিবে দুখ
এখন পরাণ যদি রহে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

hari hari gaurāṅga-biccheda nāhi sahe |
puna sei gorā-mukha dekhiyā ghucibe dukha
ekhana parāṇa yadi rahe || dhru ||

hari hari — Hari, Hari! (a cry of grief); gauranga-bichchheda — separation from Gauranga; nahi sahe — cannot be borne; puna sei gora-mukha — once more that face of Gora; dekhiya — seeing; ghuchibe dukha — the sorrow will go; ekhana parana — life now; yadi rahe — if it lasts

1.2(Refrain) Hari, Hari! Separation from Gauranga cannot be borne!
Once more we shall see Gora's face, and the sorrow will go —
if only life holds out till then.

শচীর করুণা শুনি কান্দয়ে অখিল প্রাণী
মালিনী প্রবোধ করে তায় ।
নদীয়া-নাগরীগণ কান্দে তারা অনুক্ষণ
বসন ভূষণ নাহি ভায় ॥

śacīra karuṇā śuni kāndaye akhila prāṇī
mālinī prabodha kare tāya |
nadīyā-nāgarīgaṇa kānde tārā anukṣaṇa
basana bhūṣaṇa nāhi bhāya ||

shachira karuna shuni — hearing Shachi's piteous weeping; kandaye akhila prani — every living being weeps; malini prabodha kare taya — Malini consoles her; nadiya-nagari-gana — the townswomen of Nadia; kande tara anukshana — they weep incessantly; basana bhushana — clothes and ornaments; nahi bhaya — give no pleasure

1.3Hearing Shachi's piteous weeping, every living being weeps;
Malini consoles her.3
The townswomen of Nadia weep without cease;
neither clothes nor ornaments please them.

সুরধুনী-তীরে যাইতে দেখিব গৌরাঙ্গ পথে
কত দিনে হবে শুভ দিন ।
চাঁদ-মুখের বাণী শুনি জুড়াবে তাপিত প্রাণী
গোবিন্দ ঘোষের দেহ ক্ষীণ ॥

suradhunī-tīre yāite dekhiba gaurāṅga pathe
kata dine habe śubha dina |
cām̐da-mukhera bāṇī śuni juṛābe tāpita prāṇī
gobinda ghoṣera deha kṣīṇa ||

suradhuni-tire yaite — going to the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); dekhiba gauranga pathe — we shall see Gauranga on the way; kata dine habe — after how many days will come; shubha dina — the auspicious day; chanda-mukhera bani shuni — hearing the words of [His] moon-face; jurabe tapita prani — the burning soul will be cooled; gobinda ghoshera deha kshina — Govinda Ghosha's body is wasting away

1.4When, going to the bank of the Suradhuni, shall we see Gauranga on the way —
after how many days will that auspicious day come?
We shall hear the words of His moonlike face, and the burning soul will be cooled…
Govinda Ghosha's body is wasting away.

Lord (CC Adi 10, Madhya 13). The journey to East Bengal: CB Adi 14, CC Adi 16, Murari 1.11.5–16, Lochana (Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda, part 12, vv. 61–103). Majumdar's argument: the pada has no hint of Nimai's divinity or of kirtana — the poet knows Him only as a youth he has seen on the bank of the Ganga; such simplicity is natural only in verses made before the change at Gaya. In PK the pada stands as a gaura-chandrika (prelude) to the section on "distant separation" (Krishna's departure for Mathura). Bengal she left this world, bitten by the "serpent of separation"; the pada finds her still alive, pining for her husband.

2. Vasu Ghosha — "śaṅkha dundubhi-nāda…" (BR, p. 893; PK 1536)

Lila: the abhisheka-bathing of the Lord in Srivasa's house (the mahaprakasha), 1509. According to Majumdar, the song of an eyewitness; raga bhupali (PK), suhai (BR).4

শঙ্খ দুন্দুভি-নাদ বাজয়ে সুস্বরে ।
গোরাচাঁদের অভিষেক করে সহচরে ॥

śaṅkha dundubhi-nāda bājaye susvare |
gorācām̐dera abhiṣeka kare sahacare ||

shankha — conchs; dundubhi-nada — the roll of kettledrums; bajaye susvare — sound melodiously; gorachandera — of Gorachand; abhisheka — the ceremonial bathing; kare sahachare — the companions perform

2.1Conchs and the roll of kettledrums sound melodiously:
the companions perform the abhisheka of Gorachand.

গন্ধ চন্দন শিলা ধূপ দীপ জ্বালি ।
নগরের নাগরীগণ আনে অর্ঘ্য-থালি ॥

gandha candana śilā dhūpa dīpa jvāli |
nagarera nāgarīgaṇa āne arghya-thāli ||

gandha chandana shila — fragrant sandal, the [grinding] stone; dhupa — incense; dipa jvali — lighting lamps; nagarera nagari-gana — the women of the town; ane — bring; arghya-thali — platters of arghya

2.2Fragrant sandal on the stone, incense, lamps alight;
the women of the town bring platters of arghya.5

নদীয়ার লোক যত দেখি আনন্দিত ।
ঘন জয় জয় দিয়া সভে গায় গীত ॥

nadīyāra loka yata dekhi ānandita |
ghana jaya jaya diyā sabhe gāya gīta ||

nadiyara loka yata — all the people of Nadia; dekhi anandita — rejoice to see it; ghana jaya jaya diya — crying "Jaya, jaya!" again and again; sabhe gaya gita — all sing songs

2.3All the people of Nadia look on and rejoice;
again and again they cry "Jaya, jaya!" and sing songs.

গোরাচাঁদের মুখ সভে করে নিরীক্ষণে ।
গোরা-অভিষেক-রস বাসু ঘোষ গানে ॥

gorācām̐dera mukha sabhe kare nirīkṣaṇe |
gorā-abhiṣeka-rasa bāsu ghoṣa gāne ||

gorachandera mukha — Gorachand's face; sabhe kare nirikshane — all gaze upon; gora-abhisheka-rasa — the sweetness of Gora's bathing; basu ghosha gane — Vasu Ghosha sings

2.4All gaze upon the face of Gorachand;
Vasu Ghosha sings the sweetness of Gora's abhisheka.

bathing of the Lord in Srivasa's house: CB Madhya 9; Murari 2.12; Lochana (Chaitanya-mangala, Madhya-khanda, part 9, vv. 93–113); Karnapura, Chaitanya-chandrodaya, act 1. In the Bhakti-ratnakara (wave 12) Narahari Chakravarti cites precisely this pada as an eyewitness's testimony, though he had Murari, CB and CC to hand — and on this Majumdar rests its early date. In PK it stands as a gaura-chandrika to the snana-yatra (the bathing of Jagannatha at the full moon of Jyeshtha). detail the biographies pass over — the part women took in the rite.

3. Vasu Ghosha — "taila haridrā āra kuṅkuma kastūrī…" (PK 1537)

Lila: the same abhisheka — the anointing, bathing and dressing of the Lord. Raga varadi.6

তৈল হরিদ্রা আর কুঙ্কুম কস্তূরী ।
গোরা-অঙ্গে লেপন করে নব নব নারী ॥

taila haridrā āra kuṅkuma kastūrī |
gorā-aṅge lepana kare naba naba nārī ||

taila — oil; haridra — turmeric; ara kunkuma kasturi — and kunkuma, musk; gora-ange — on Gora's body; lepana kare — apply; naba naba nari — women, one after another

3.1Oil, turmeric, kunkuma and musk
the women, one after another, apply to Gora's body.

সুবাসিত জল আনি কলসে পূরিয়া ।
সুগন্ধি চন্দন আদি তাহে মিশাইয়া ॥

subāsita jala āni kalase pūriyā |
sugandhi candana ādi tāhe miśāiyā ||

subasita jala ani — bringing scented water; kalase puriya — filling the pitchers; sugandhi chandana adi — fragrant sandal and the like; tahe mishaiya — mixing into it

3.2Bringing scented water, they fill the pitchers
and mix fragrant sandal and other things into it.

জয় জয় দিয়া জল ঢালে গোরা-গায় ।
শ্রীঅঙ্গ মোছাঞা কেহ বসন পরায় ॥

jaya jaya diyā jala ḍhāle gorā-gāya |
śrīaṅga mochāñā keha basana parāya ||

jaya jaya diya — crying "Jaya, jaya!"; jala dhale gora-gaya — they pour water over Gora's body; shri-anga mochhana — wiping the holy body; keha basana paraya — someone dresses [Him] in garments

3.3Crying "Jaya, jaya!" they pour the water over Gora's body;
wiping the holy body, someone dresses Him in garments.

সিনান-মণ্ডপে দেখ গোরা নটরায় ।
মনের হরিষে বাসুদেব ঘোষ গায় ॥

sināna-maṇḍape dekha gorā naṭarāya |
manera hariṣe bāsudeba ghoṣa gāya ||

sinana-mandape — in the bathing pavilion; dekha — behold!; gora nataraya — Gora, king of dancers; manera harishe — with joy at heart; vasudeva ghosha gaya — Vasudeva Ghosha sings

3.4Behold, in the bathing pavilion — Gora, king of dancers!
With joy at heart Vasudeva Ghosha sings.

1509 (PK 1536, 1537, 1571 — the "historical" padas of Vasu Ghosha). "King of dancers" (nata-raya) is a frequent name for Gaura, the leader of the dancers in kirtana, among the kirtana poets.

4. Govinda, Madhava and Vasu Ghosha — "basilā gaurāṅgacandra ratna-siṃhāsane…" (PK 1538)

Lila: after the abhisheka the Lord on the throne: the feast, Shachi's arati, the worship of the devotees. Signed by all three Ghosha brothers.7

বসিলা গৌরাঙ্গচন্দ্র রত্ন-সিংহাসনে ।
শ্রীবাস পণ্ডিত অঙ্গে লেপয়ে চন্দন ॥

basilā gaurāṅgacandra ratna-siṃhāsane |
śrībāsa paṇḍita aṅge lepaye candana ||

basila gauranga-chandra — Gaurangachandra sat; ratna-simhasane — on the jewelled throne; shribasa pandita — Srivasa Pandita; ange lepaye chandana — anoints His body with sandal

4.1Gaurangachandra sat upon the jewelled throne;
Srivasa Pandita anoints His body with sandal.

গদাধর দিল গলে মালতীর মালা ।
রূপের ছটায় দশ দিগ হৈল আলা ॥

gadādhara dila gale mālatīra mālā |
rūpera chaṭāya daśa diga haila ālā ||

gadadhara dila gale — Gadadhara placed on His neck; malatira mala — a garland of malati; rupera chhataya — by the radiance of His beauty; dasha diga haila ala — the ten directions were lit up

4.2Gadadhara placed a garland of malati on His neck;
by the radiance of His beauty all ten directions were lit.

বহু উপহার যত মিষ্টান্ন পকার ।
নিত্যানন্দ সহ বসি করিল ভোজন ॥

bahu upahāra yata miṣṭānna pakāra |
nityānanda saha basi karila bhojana ||

bahu upahara — many offerings; yata mishtanna pakara — every kind of sweet dish; nityananda saha basi — sitting with Nityananda; karila bhojana — He ate

4.3Many offerings, every kind of sweet dish
He ate, sitting together with Nityananda.

তাম্বূল ভক্ষণ করি বসিলা সিংহাসনে ।
শচী দেবী আইলেন মালিনীর সনে ॥

tāmbūla bhakṣaṇa kari basilā siṃhāsane |
śacī debī āilena mālinīra sane ||

tambula bhakshana kari — having chewed tambula (betel); basila simhasane — He sat on the throne; shachi devi ailena — Shachi-devi came; malinira sane — with Malini

4.4Having chewed tambula, He sat on the throne again;
Shachi-devi came together with Malini.

পঞ্চদীপ জ্বালি তেঁহ আরাত্রিক কৈল ।
নিরমঞ্ছন করি শিরে ধান্য দূর্বা দিল ॥

pañcadīpa jvāli tem̐ha ārātrika kaila |
niramañchana kari śire dhānya dūrvā dila ||

panchadipa jvali — lighting the five-wicked lamp; tenha aratrika kaila — she performed arati; nirmanchhana kari — waving [it] round; shire — on His head; dhanya durva dila — she placed paddy and durva grass

4.5Lighting the five-wicked lamp, she performed arati,
waved [the flame] round Him and placed paddy and durva on His head.8

তৎক্ষণ করে সভে পুষ্প বরিষণ ।
অদ্বৈত আচার্য দেই তুলসী চন্দন ॥

tatkṣaṇa kare sabhe puṣpa bariṣaṇa |
advaita ācārya dei tulasī candana ||

tatkshana — at that moment; kare sabhe pushpa barishana — all shower flowers; advaita acharya — Advaita Acharya; dei tulasi chandana — offers tulasi and sandal

4.6At that moment all shower Him with flowers;
Advaita Acharya offers tulasi and sandal.

দেখিতে আইসে দেব নরে এক সঙ্গে ।
নিত্যানন্দ ডাহিনে বসিয়া দেখে রঙ্গে ॥

dekhite āise deba nare eka saṅge |
nityānanda ḍāhine basiyā dekhe raṅge ||

dekhite aise — come to see; deba nare eka sange — gods and men together; nityananda dahine basiya — Nityananda, sitting on the right; dekhe range — watches with delight

4.7Gods and men come together to see it;
Nityananda, sitting at His right, watches with delight.

গোরা-অভিষেক এই অপরূপ লীলা ।
গোবিন্দ মাধব বাসু প্রেমেতে ভাসিলা ॥

gorā-abhiṣeka ei aparūpa līlā |
gobinda mādhaba bāsu premete bhāsilā ||

gora-abhisheka — Gora's bathing; ei aparupa lila — this matchless lila; gobinda madhava basu — Govinda, Madhava [and] Vasu; premete bhasila — floated away in prema

4.8This is the matchless lila of Gora's abhisheka:
Govinda, Madhava and Vasu floated away in prema.

house; from the signature "Govinda, Madhava, Vasu" (as in Vasu Ramananda) he infers that Govinda was the eldest. The Lord sitting on Vishnu's throne in Srivasa's house, accepting offerings and receiving the devotees' worship: CB Madhya 9; CC Adi 17.

5. Ramachandra — "pahu mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (BR, p. 919; PK 2186)

Lila: the Lord in Navadvipa in the mood of Radha, with Gadadhara and Narahari beside Him. According to Majumdar, the song of an eyewitness (Narahari Chakravarti cites it as testimony). Raga shri (PK), suhai (BR).9

পহু মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
শিব শুক বিরিঞ্চি যার গুণ গায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

pahu mora gaurāṅga rāya |
śiba śuka biriñci yāra guṇa gāya || dhru ||

pahu mora — my Lord; gauranga raya — Gauranga Raya; shiva shuka virinchi — Shiva, Shuka, Brahma; yara guna gaya — whose qualities sing

5.1(Refrain) My Lord is Gauranga Raya,
whose glories Shiva, Shuka and Brahma sing!

কমলা যাহার ভাবে সদাই আকুলি ।
সেই পহু বাহু তুলি কান্দে হরি বলি ॥

kamalā yāhāra bhābe sadāi ākuli |
sei pahu bāhu tuli kānde hari bali ||

kamala — Kamala (Lakshmi); yahara bhabe — in love for whom; sadai akuli — is ever restless; sei pahu — that same Lord; bahu tuli — raising His arms; kande hari bali — weeps, crying "Hari!"

5.2He for whom Kamala ever pines,10
that very Lord raises His arms, weeps and cries out, "Hari!"

যে অঙ্গ হেরি হেরি অনঙ্গ ভেল কাম ।
সো অব কীর্তন-ধূলি-ধূসর অবিরাম ॥

ye aṅga heri heri anaṅga bhela kāma |
so aba kīrtana-dhūli-dhūsara abirāma ||

ye anga — the body which; heri heri — beholding again and again; ananga bhela kama — Kama became bodiless; so aba — that now; kirtana-dhuli-dhusara — grey with the dust of kirtana; abirama — unceasingly

5.3The body at whose sight Kamadeva became bodiless11
is now ever grey with the dust of kirtana.

খেণে রাধা রাধা বলি উঠে চমকিয়া ।
গদাধর নরহরি রহে মুখ চাঞা ॥

kheṇe rādhā rādhā bali uṭhe camakiyā |
gadādhara narahari rahe mukha cāñā ||

khene — now and then; radha radha bali — crying "Radha, Radha!"; uthe chamakiya — He starts up; gadadhara narahari — Gadadhara [and] Narahari; rahe mukha chana — stand gazing at [His] face

5.4Now and again He starts up, crying, "Radha, Radha!" —
Gadadhara and Narahari stand gazing at His face.

পুরব-নিবিড়-প্রেম-পুলকিত অঙ্গ ।
রামচন্দ্র কহে কে না বুঝে ও না রঙ্গ ॥

puraba-nibiṛa-prema-pulakita aṅga |
rāmacandra kahe ke nā bujhe o nā raṅga ||

puraba-nibira-prema — with the deep love of old; pulakita anga — His body thrills; ramachandra kahe — says Ramachandra; ke na bujhe — who would not understand; o na ranga — that play

5.5His body thrills with the deep love of former days.
Says Ramachandra: who would not understand this play?

Khan, and suggests Ramachandra Kaviraja of Nityananda's branch (not Narottama's friend, whom Narahari Chakravarti would not have passed off as an eyewitness). In BR (wave 12) the pada stands among testimonies to the Navadvipa pastimes, directly after Govinda Ghosha's pada on the Lord's dancing with Narahari. Narahari Sarakara Thakura (of Shrikhanda) was a singer of Gaura's moods; Majumdar confirms his presence with the Lord in Navadvipa from the padas of other contemporaries. Cf. CC Adi 17 (Radha's mood in Navadvipa). (Lakshmi longs for the dust of Krishna's feet). Bodiless", is his name). The "love of former days" (v. 5.5) is Radha's love for Krishna, which the Lord tastes in the form of Gaura. BR reads: "He gazes at the faces of Narahari and Gadadhara."

6. Murari Gupta — "gadādhara-aṅge pahu aṅga helāiyā…" (BR, p. 922; PK 2121)

Lila: the Lord in Radha's mood, leaning on Gadadhara, listens to the song of Vrindavana. According to Majumdar, composed in 1509 under the immediate impression of Nimai's moods. Raga patamanjari (PK), kamoda (BR).12

গদাধর-অঙ্গে পহু অঙ্গ হেলাইয়া ।
বৃন্দাবন-গুণ গান বিভোর হইয়া ॥

gadādhara-aṅge pahu aṅga helāiyā |

Chakravarti introduces them as songs composed at the very places in Navadvipa that are shown to Srinivasa Acharya on his circuit of Navadvipa ("here, under this kadamba, Gora, dressed as Natavara and standing thrice-bent, played the flute"). Majumdar takes them as describing what was seen with one's own eyes in 1509. "A snare for the women" (9.5) is a poetic image of the Lord's irresistible beauty (Krishna the Natavara captivates the gopis); Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never so much as glanced at another man's wife, and the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari".

tora preme bandi haiya — captive to your love; berainu bharamiya — I wandered about; rahite narinu nilachale — I could not stay in Nilachala; tore dekhibara tare — to see you; ainu nadiyapure — I came to Nadia; kandite kandite iha bole — weeping, He says this

22.3"Captive to your love, I wandered about —
I could not stay in Nilachala.
To see you I have come to Nadia" —
so He says, weeping.

আইস মোর বাছা বুলি হিয়ার উপরে তুলি
হেন বেলে নিদ দূরে গেল ।
পুন না দেখিয়া তারে পরাণ কেমন করে
কান্দিয়া রজনী পোহাইল ॥

āisa mora bāchā buli hiyāra upare tuli
hena bele nida dūre gela |
puna nā dekhiyā tāre parāṇa kemana kare
kāndiyā rajanī pohāila ||

aisa mora bachha buli — saying "Come, my child!"; hiyara upare tuli — I lifted Him to my breast; hena bele — at that moment; nida dure gela — sleep went away; puna na dekhiya tare — not seeing Him again; parana kemana kare — how my heart aches!; kandiya rajani pohaila — the night passed in tears

22.4"Come to me, my child!" — I lifted Him to my breast —
and at that moment sleep left me.
Not seeing Him again, how my heart aches!
The night passed in tears.

কান্দিতে কান্দিতে শচী মুরছি পড়ল ক্ষিতি
মালিনী কান্দয়ে উভরায় ।
কি বলিব হায় হায় এ দুখ না সহে গায়
বাসু কেনে মরিয়া না যায় ॥

kāndite kāndite śacī murachi paṛala kṣiti
mālinī kāndaye ubharāya |
ki baliba hāya hāya e dukha nā sahe gāya
bāsu kene mariyā nā yāya ||

kandite kandite shachi — weeping and weeping, Shachi; murachhi parala kshiti — fell fainting to the ground; malini kandaye ubharaya — Malini wails aloud; ki baliba haya haya — what can I say, alas!; e dukha na sahe gaya — this pain cannot be borne; basu kene mariya na yaya — why does Vasu not die?

22.5Weeping and weeping, Shachi fell fainting to the ground;
Malini wails aloud.
What can I say — alas, alas! — this pain cannot be borne:
why does Vasu not die?

Nityananda comes. Majumdar values this and the next pada as testimonies which the later biographers left out, as if they "diminished" the sannyasa. Cf. CC Antya 3: the Lord says that He comes unseen to eat what Shachi cooks. Addendum (chapter 05): the same pada is found in PK — no. 2270 (vol. 3, PDF p. 293, printed p. 282; 21st pallava, raga vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 2374) and in GPT1 (p. 386, no. 11, raga pahida) — signed by Vasudeva Ghosha and with a different last stanza: "Since then my soul weeps, my heart finds no rest: what shall I do, tell me, what way is there? Says Vasudeva Ghosha: Gauranga is yours — otherwise would you always see Him?" Stanzas 22.1–22.4 in PK have minor variants (see the full version of the book). PK 2268 "biraha-bikala māya…", which the stage-1 catalogue took for this pada (VG-138), is a pada of Premadasa.

23. Vasu Ghosha — "āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite…" (GPT1, p. 413)

Lila: the sannyasi Chaitanya comes to Nadia (1514/15); the people of Navadvipa and Mother Shachi see Him. Raga shri.35

আওল নদীয়ার লোক গৌরাঙ্গ দেখিতে ।
আনন্দে আকুল চিত না পারে চলিতে ॥

āola nadīyāra loka gaurāṅga dekhite |
ānande ākula cita nā pāre calite ||

aola nadiyara loka — the people of Nadia came; gauranga dekhite — to see Gauranga; anande akula chita — their hearts overwhelmed with joy; na pare chalite — they cannot walk

23.1The people of Nadia came to see Gauranga:
their hearts so overwhelmed with joy they cannot walk.

চিরদিনে গোরাচাঁদের বদন দেখিয়া ।
ভুখিল চকোর আঁখি রহয়ে মাতিয়া ॥

ciradine gorācām̐dera badana dekhiyā |
bhukhila cakora ām̐khi rahaye mātiyā ||

chiradine — after so long; gorachandera badana dekhiya — seeing Gorachand's face; bhukhila chakora ankhi — the hungry chakora-eyes; rahaye matiya — remain intoxicated

23.2Seeing Gorachand's face after so long,
their hungry chakora-eyes are intoxicated.

আনন্দে ভকতগণ হেরিয়া বিভোর ।
জননী ধাইয়া গোরাচাঁদে করে কোর ॥

ānande bhakatagaṇa heriyā bibhora |
jananī dhāiyā gorācām̐de kare kora ||

anande bhakatagana — the devotees, in joy; heriya bibhora — are lost in gazing; janani dhaiya — the mother, running up; gorachande kare kora — embraces Gorachand

23.3The devotees are lost in joy, gazing at Him;
the mother runs up and embraces Gorachand.

মরণ-শরীরে যেন পাইল পরাণ ।
গৌরাঙ্গ নদীয়াপুরে বাসু ঘোষ গান ॥

maraṇa-śarīre yena pāila parāṇa |
gaurāṅga nadīyāpure bāsu ghoṣa gāna ||

marana-sharire — into a dying body; yena paila parana — as if life returned; gauranga nadiyapure — Gauranga in Nadia; basu ghosha gana — Vasu Ghosha sings

23.4As if life had returned to a dying body:
Gauranga is in Nadia, sings Vasu Ghosha.

to the neighbourhood of Navadvipa on His way to Gauda (1514/15), told by Murari (4.14.3–11) and Lochana (Shesha-khanda); CC (Madhya 1) and CB (Antya 3) speak of His stay at Kuliya, opposite Navadvipa. The chakora is a bird that, in poetic tradition, feeds on moonlight.

24. Krishnadasa — "ṭhākura paṇḍitera bāṛī gorā nāce phiri phiri…" (PK 2358)

Lila: the Lord and Nityananda at Ambika with Gauridasa Pandita; Gauridasa begs Them to stay, and the Lord tells him to serve Their Deities. According to Majumdar, a contemporary testimony that the worship of the Lord's Deity began in His lifetime. Raga bhatiyari.36

ঠাকুর পণ্ডিতের বাড়ী গোরা নাচে ফিরি ফিরি
নিত্যানন্দ বলে হরি হরি ।
কান্দি গৌরীদাস বলে পড়ি প্রভুর পদ-তলে
কভু না ছাড়িবে মোর বাড়ী ॥

ṭhākura paṇḍitera bāṛī gorā nāce phiri phiri
nityānanda bale hari hari |
kāndi gaurīdāsa bale paṛi prabhura pada-tale
kabhu nā chāṛibe mora bāṛī ||

thakura panditera bari — in Thakura Pandita's house; gora nache phiri phiri — Gora dances, whirling round; nityananda bale hari hari — Nityananda cries "Hari, Hari!"; kandi gauridasa bale — weeping, Gauridasa says; pari prabhura pada-tale — falling at the Lord's feet; kabhu na chharibe mora bari — "Never leave my house!"

24.1In Thakura Pandita's house Gora dances, whirling round;
Nityananda cries, "Hari, Hari!"
Weeping, Gauridasa falls at the Lord's feet and says:
"Never leave my house!

আমার বচন রাখ অম্বিকানগরে থাক
এই নিবেদন তুয়া পায় ।
যদি ছাড়ি যাবে তুমি নিশ্চয় মরিব আমি
রহিব সে নিরখিয়া কায় ॥

āmāra bacana rākha ambikānagare thāka
ei nibedana tuyā pāya |
yadi chāṛi yābe tumi niścaya mariba āmi
rahiba se nirakhiyā kāya ||

amara bachana rakha — grant my request; ambika-nagare thaka — stay in Ambika; ei nibedana tuya paya — this is my plea at Your feet; yadi chhari yabe tumi — if You leave; nishchaya mariba ami — I shall surely die; rahiba se nirakhiya kaya — looking at whom shall I live?

24.2Grant my request — stay in Ambika:
this is my plea at Your feet.
If You go away, I shall surely die:
looking at whom shall I live then?

তোমরা যে দুটি ভাই থাক মোর এই ঠাঞি
তবে সভার হয় পরিত্রাণ ।
পুন নিবেদন করি না ছাড়িহ গৌরহরি
তবে জানি পতিত-পাবন ॥

tomarā ye duṭi bhāi thāka mora ei ṭhāñi
tabe sabhāra haya paritrāṇa |
puna nibedana kari nā chāṛiha gaurahari
tabe jāni patita-pābana ||

tomara ye duti bhai — you two brothers; thaka mora ei thani — stay here with me; tabe sabhara haya paritrana — then all will be delivered; puna nibedana kari — again I pray; na chhariha gaurahari — do not leave [me], Gaurahari; tabe jani patita-pabana — then I shall know You are the saviour of the fallen

24.3If You two brothers stay here with me,
then everyone will be delivered.
Again I pray: do not leave me, Gaurahari —
then I shall know that You are the saviour of the fallen."

প্রভু কহে গৌরীদাস ছাড়হ এমত আশ
প্রতিমূর্তি সেবা করি দেখ ।
তাহাতে আছিয়ে আমি নিশ্চয় জানিহ তুমি
সত্য মোর এই বাক্য রাখ ॥

prabhu kahe gaurīdāsa chāṛaha emata āśa
pratimūrti sebā kari dekha |
tāhāte āchiye āmi niścaya jāniha tumi
satya mora ei bākya rākha ||

prabhu kahe gauridasa — the Lord says, "Gauridasa!; chharaha emata asha — give up such a wish; pratimurti seba kari dekha — serve [My] image and see; tahate achhiye ami — I am present in it; nishchaya janiha tumi — know this for certain; satya mora ei bakya rakha — keep this true word of Mine"

24.4The Lord says: "Gauridasa, give up such a wish:
serve My Deity and you will see —
I am present in it, know this for certain;
keep this true word of Mine."

এত শুনি গৌরীদাস ছাড়ি দীর্ঘ নিশ্বাস
ফুকরি ফুকরি পুন কান্দে ।
পুন সেই দুই ভাই প্রবোধ করয়ে তায়
তবু হিয়া থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

eta śuni gaurīdāsa chāṛi dīrgha niśvāsa
phukari phukari puna kānde |
puna sei dui bhāi prabodha karaye tāya
tabu hiyā thira nāhi bāndhe ||

eta shuni gauridasa — hearing this, Gauridasa; chhari dirgha nishvasa — heaving a long sigh; phukari phukari puna kande — again weeps aloud; puna sei dui bhai — again the two brothers; prabodha karaye taya — console him; tabu hiya thira nahi bandhe — yet his heart finds no rest

24.5Hearing this, Gauridasa heaved a long sigh
and again weeps aloud.
Again the two brothers console him,
yet his heart finds no rest.

কহে দীন কৃষ্ণদাস চৈতন্য-চরণে আশ
দুই ভাই রহিলা তথায় ।
ঠাকুর পণ্ডিতের প্রেমে বন্দী হৈলা দুই জনে
ভকত-বৎসল তেঞি গায় ॥

kahe dīna kṛṣṇadāsa caitanya-caraṇe āśa
dui bhāi rahilā tathāya |
ṭhākura paṇḍitera preme bandī hailā dui jane
bhakata-batsala teñi gāya ||

kahe dina krishnadasa — says lowly Krishnadasa; chaitanya-charane asha — whose hope is Chaitanya's feet; dui bhai rahila tathaya — the two brothers stayed there; thakura panditera preme — by Thakura Pandita's love; bandi haila dui jane — both became captives; bhakata-batsala tenyi gaya — hence they are sung as loving to their devotees

24.6Says lowly Krishnadasa, whose hope is Chaitanya's feet:
the two brothers stayed there.
Both were taken captive by Thakura Pandita's love —
hence They are sung as "loving to Their devotees".37

Pandita (here "Thakura Pandita") was a companion of Nityananda, Subala according to GGD; at Ambika-Kalna he served the Deities of Gaura-Nitai. Cf. Murari 4.14.12–14. Majumdar's argument: the pada is a contemporary's testimony that the worship of the Lord's Deity began in His lifetime. The next pada of PK (2359) continues the story. Their own word, They Themselves are present: the Deity is not an image but the Lord Himself, manifest through the devotee's love.

25. Chandrashekhara — "kṣaṇeka rahiyā caliyā uṭhiyā paṇḍita jagadānanda…" (PK 1854)

Lila: Jagadananda Pandita comes from Nilachala to Navadvipa, to Shachi and Vishnupriya. According to Majumdar, written "before one's eyes", in the Lord's lifetime.38

ক্ষণেক রহিয়া চলিয়া উঠিয়া
পণ্ডিত জগদানন্দ ।
প্রবেশি নগরে দেখে ঘরে ঘরে
লোক সব নিরানন্দ ॥

kṣaṇeka rahiyā caliyā uṭhiyā
paṇḍita jagadānanda |
prabeśi nagare dekhe ghare ghare
loka saba nirānanda ||

kshaneka rahiya — after pausing a while; chaliya uthiya — rising and going on; pandita jagadananda — Pandita Jagadananda; prabeshi nagare — entering the town; dekhe ghare ghare — sees that in every house; loka saba nirananda — all the people are joyless

25.1After pausing a while, Pandita Jagadananda
rose and went on.
Entering the town, he sees that in every house
all the people are joyless.

না মেলে পসার না করে আহার
কারো মুখে নাহি হাসি ।
নগরে নাগরী কান্দয়ে গুমরি
থাকয়ে বিরলে বসি ॥

nā mele pasāra nā kare āhāra
kāro mukhe nāhi hāsi |
nagare nāgarī kāndaye gumari
thākaye birale basi ||

na mele pasara — the shops are not open; na kare ahara — no one eats; karo mukhe nahi hasi — no smile on any face; nagare nagari — the women of the town; kandaye gumari — weep with stifled sobs; thakaye birale basi — sit apart in solitude

25.2The shops are not open, no one eats,
no face has a smile.
The women of the town weep with stifled sobs,
sitting apart, alone.

দেখিয়া নগর ঠাকুরের ঘর
প্রবেশ করল যাই ।
আধ মরা হেন ভূমে অচেতন
পড়িয়া আছেন আই ॥

dekhiyā nagara ṭhākurera ghara
prabeśa karala yāi |
ādha marā hena bhūme acetana
paṛiyā āchena āi ||

dekhiya nagara — having seen the town; thakurera ghara — the Lord's house; prabesha karala yai — he went and entered; adha mara hena — as if half dead; bhume achetana — senseless on the ground; pariya achhena ai — lies Ai (Mother Shachi)

25.3Having seen the town, he went
and entered the Lord's house.
As if half dead, senseless,
Ai lies on the ground.39

প্রভুর রমণী সেহ অনাথিনী
প্রভুরে হইয়া হারা ।
পড়িয়া আছেন মলিন বসন
মুদল-নয়ানে ধারা ॥

prabhura ramaṇī seha anāthinī
prabhure haiyā hārā |
paṛiyā āchena malina basana
mudala-nayāne dhārā ||

prabhura ramani — the Lord's wife; seha anathini — she too, forsaken; prabhure haiya hara — having lost the Lord; pariya achhena — lies; malina basana — in faded clothes; mudala-nayane dhara — tears from closed eyes

25.4And the Lord's wife, forsaken,
having lost the Lord,
lies in faded clothes,
tears flowing from her closed eyes.

দাস দাসী সব আছয়ে নীরব
দেখিয়া পথিক-জন ।
সোধাইছে তারে কহ দেখি মোরে
কোথা হৈতে আগমন ॥

dāsa dāsī saba āchaye nīraba
dekhiyā pathika-jana |
sodhāiche tāre kaha dekhi more
kothā haite āgamana ||

dasa dasi saba — all the servants and maids; achhaye niraba — are silent; dekhiya pathika-jana — seeing the traveller; sodhaichhe tare — they ask him; kaha dekhi more — tell me now; kotha haite agamana — where have you come from?

25.5All the servants and maids are silent;
seeing the traveller,
they ask him: "Tell us now,
where have you come from?"

পণ্ডিত কহেন মোর আগমন
নীলাচলপুর হৈতে ।
গৌরাঙ্গ-সুন্দর পাঠাইল মোরে
তোমা সভারে দেখিতে ॥

paṇḍita kahena mora āgamana
nīlācalapura haite |
gaurāṅga-sundara pāṭhāila more
tomā sabhāre dekhite ||

pandita kahena — the Pandita says; mora agamana — I have come; nilachalapura haite — from Nilachala; gauranga-sundara pathaila more — beautiful Gauranga sent me; toma sabhare dekhite — to see you all

25.6The Pandita says: "I have come
from Nilachala.
Beautiful Gauranga sent me
to see you all."

শুনিয়া বচন সজল নয়ন
শচীরে কহল গিয়া ।
আর এক জন চলিল তখন
শ্রীবাস-মন্দিরে ধাঞা ॥

śuniyā bacana sajala nayana
śacīre kahala giyā |
āra eka jana calila takhana
śrībāsa-mandire dhāñā ||

shuniya bachana — hearing these words; sajala nayana — with tearful eyes; shachire kahala giya — they went and told Shachi; ara eka jana — and another; chalila takhana — set off at once; shribasa-mandire dhana — running to Srivasa's house

25.7Hearing these words, with tearful eyes
they went and told Shachi,
and another set off at once
running to Srivasa's house.

শুনিয়া শ্রীবাস মালিনী উল্লাস
যত নবদ্বীপ-বাসী ।
মরা হেন ছিল অমনি ধাইল
পরাণ পাইল আসি ॥

śuniyā śrībāsa mālinī ullāsa
yata nabadvīpa-bāsī |
marā hena chila amani dhāila
parāṇa pāila āsi ||

shuniya shribasa — hearing it, Srivasa; malini ullasa — Malini overjoyed; yata nabadvipa-basi — and all the people of Navadvipa; mara hena chhila — had been as if dead; amani dhaila — at once they ran; parana paila asi — coming, they came back to life

25.8Hearing it, Srivasa, Malini in delight,
and all the people of Navadvipa,
who had been as if dead, came running at once —
and, coming, came back to life.

মালিনী আসিয়া শচী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া
উঠাইল যতন করি ।
তাহারে কহিল পণ্ডিত আইল
পাঠাইল গৌরহরি ॥

mālinī āsiyā śacī biṣṇupriyā
uṭhāila yatana kari |
tāhāre kahila paṇḍita āila
pāṭhāila gaurahari ||

malini asiya — Malini, coming; shachi vishnupriya — Shachi [and] Vishnupriya; uthaila yatana kari — gently raised; tahare kahila — told them; pandita aila — the Pandita has come; pathaila gaurahari — Gaurahari has sent him

25.9Malini came and gently raised
Shachi and Vishnupriya
and told them: "The Pandita has come;
Gaurahari has sent him."

শুনি শচী আই সচকিত চাই
দেখিলেন পণ্ডিতেরে ।
কহে তার ঠাই আমার নিমাই
আসিয়াছে কত দূরে ॥

śuni śacī āi sacakita cāi
dekhilena paṇḍitere |
kahe tāra ṭhāi āmāra nimāi
āsiyāche kata dūre ||

shuni shachi ai — hearing it, Mother Shachi; sachakita chai — looked up with a start; dekhilena panditere — saw the Pandita; kahe tara thai — says to him; amara nimai — my Nimai; asiyachhe kata dure — how far off has He come?

25.10Hearing it, Mother Shachi looked up with a start
and saw the Pandita.
